metadata.title: Amazon, alternative carriers gained parcel volume in 2026’s first half

content.text:
This story was originally published on Supply Chain Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily Supply Chain Dive newsletter.
Dive Brief:
-
Amazon posted a 9.7% increase in U.S. parcel deliveries in the first half of 2026 versus the same period in 2025 as the e-commerce giant relied less on UPS for shipping and ramped up its rural delivery coverage, according to an Oct. 27 news release from ShipMatrix, a shipping consultancy and analytics provider.
-
UPS' volume dropped 5.7% over the same stretch amid the carrier's planned Amazon delivery decline, ShipMatrix said. In June, UPS wrapped up a plan first announced in 2025 to slash its Amazon volume in half as the company pursued more profitable packages in other categories.
-
Amazon's 2026 growth adds to the company's market share gains in the parcel delivery space over the past several years. Last year, Amazon's logistics arm surpassed the U.S. Postal Service as the top U.S. parcel carrier by volume, although it still lagged behind UPS and FedEx in terms of market share by revenue, according to ShipMatrix data released in March.
Dive Insight:
Amazon's delivery activity has seen another big leap this year as the company works to rely less on outside partners such as UPS and the Postal Service. Amazon is also driving more shippers to use its delivery services through Amazon Shipping, which opened up to all customers earlier this year and has taken an aggressive pricing approach to boost volume.
Meanwhile, the Postal Service logged a 3.1% volume decline from H1 2025 to H1 2026, according to ShipMatrix data. While the agency has seen volume gains in its Ground Advantage service this year, other package shipping categories like Parcel Services and Priority Mail have posted declines, per the Postal Service's most recent earnings report. Postmaster General David Steiner has expressed an interest in the USPS pursuing heavier, higher-value packages to help improve its financial outlook.
On the other hand, FedEx posted a 4.6% increase in U.S. parcel volume over the same period as the carrier gained momentum in higher-value customer segments like automotive and healthcare.
Lost volumes from UPS and the Postal Service didn't exclusively result in market share gains for Amazon and FedEx's networks, according to ShipMatrix. An additional 145 million packages went to alternative carriers like OnTrac, Veho, Jitsu, DoorDash, SpeedX and UniUni, per the news release. The in-house networks of large retailers like Walmart also gained a portion of those diverted packages.
